g.text: Section through one rib, square to the slope, 1:10

svg.text: Roof grid A: ruled-surface columns
one roof face seen square on
(1) Columns run in straight lines from the base edge (every 1050)
towards the crown edge, so they converge like the ruled surface of
the sketch.
(2) When the spacing drops to 500 (about +6.13) every other column
stops; at about +7.77 only the four hip columns go on to the crown
ring.
(3*) Rib (column): a channel 160 wide x 240 deep printed in the
160 air zone + layer 2 stays in place as formwork and is filled
with cast concrete, 4 Ø16 + Ø8 stirrups every 200 (assumed). Fibre
concrete could replace the bars (see notes).
(4) Inner layer 1, 80: continuous, covers the grid on the room
side.
(5) Outer skin 80: continuous, covers the grid on the outside
(cladding on it).
(6*) Between the ribs the air zone stays open for thermal
insulation (dotted).
(7) Printed wall 400 (same layers as the roof), to +2.50.
(8) Buttresses 400 wide, 1000 from the inner face (600 outside),
at the corners and mid-span; roof ribs and wall bars tie into the
solid base above them.
(9*) Strip footing 1800 x 250, underside at -1.00 (hidden,
dashed): printed edge formwork, cast core.
(10) Printed channel walls, 80 each side of the rib: permanent
formwork, printed in the same pass as the shell.
* = assumed, to confirm
Notes
Columns stop on a horizontal rib (at 3626 and 5275 above
the eave); bars are lapped / hooked into it.
Horizontal ribs at 1813, 3626, 5275, plus the 300 solid
base (bottom ring) and the top ring at the crown.
All 3D printed (after the Obayashi 3dpod paper, 2023):
mortar beads are printed as permanent formwork, in 10 mm
layers (joints drawn every 100 on the elevation), and the
structural concrete is cast into them in lifts limited by
formwork pressure; the shell, wall and buttress faces are
the printed skin.
The paper fills the formwork with self-compacting
steel-fibre UHPC (about 180 N/mm2 compression, 8.8
tension) and needs no rebar in principle; if you use it,
the Ø16 bars in the ribs can be dropped or cut back, to be
confirmed with the engineer.
Rough quantities, four faces (hips counted twice, so
slightly high): ribs 325 m, 4 Ø16 each bars, steel 2049
kg, cast concrete 12.5 m3.
Rib size, bar count and the 160 x 240 channel are
assumptions for the engineer to check. Elevation shows the
face square on; true lengths are 1.25 x the drawn heights.
m
Scale 1:50 at A3 · dimensions in mm · draft 1, 2026-10-11
pyramid-roof · hand estimates, not engineered
